Three challenges

As agents produce more code, the hard part is keeping their work visible, trustworthy and reviewable.

Visibility

Know what every agent is doing and what is left before you ship. Today, that means piecing together terminals, chat logs and branches.

Trust

An agent saying “done” is only the beginning. You need evidence that the change works and meets your team’s definition of done.

Review load

Several agents can build at once. Your attention is still finite. Bring the work and its evidence together so you can make one clear decision.

The delivery model

The unit of work is the delivery

Agents run the loop. Blume keeps the record. You step in when there is a verified revision to approve.

One product change with its brief, task tree, agent runs, code revision, tests and screenshots, intact from the first instruction to production.

Interactive product preview · Illustrative data

What you get

Output, confidence, quality

The process tells agents what “done” means, and every claim arrives with its evidence.

  • Output

    Agents work longer without supervision, and several can work in parallel without silent collisions.

    How The delivery model lets agents coordinate, and the agentic loop lets the agent catch issues before involving you.

  • Confidence

    Every claim has evidence tied to a specific revision. You see what’s left at a glance.

    How Evidence is pinned to the exact task, delivery and commit. Visual verification at zero friction.

  • Quality

    Acceptance criteria become tests before review, and suites rerun before every review.

    How Bug reports are reproduced with a failing test first, then fixed and rerun.

Your product, understood before work begins

A shared, versioned domain model gives every agent the same language, rules and edge cases. Each session starts with your team’s context, not a blank slate.

Your product’s working knowledge One model, shaped by real work

  1. Language

    Entities, relationships and the words your team uses

  2. Rules

    Business invariants, permissions and boundaries

  3. Journeys

    Critical paths and their expected outcomes

  4. Risks

    Known edge cases across time zones and currencies

  5. Architecture

    Conventions and patterns agents must preserve

Reviewed decisions, findings and bug reproductions keep it current as your product changes.
